'''''Kalanchoe sexangularis''''', also known as '''bushveld kalanchoe''', '''six-angled kalanchoe''', or '''red-leaved kalanchoe''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Crassulaceae]] that is native to [[Southern Africa]].

==Description==
[[File:Kalanchoe_sexangularis.jpg|thumb|180px|left|Leaves]]
[[File:Kalanchoe_sexangularis_flowers.jpg|thumb|180px|left|Flowers]]
''Kalanchoe sexangularis'' is a [[succulent]], [[perennial]]  that reaches heights of 20 to 100 centimeters. Its single or few simple, upright, round, reddish shoots are somewhat two-to-six-sided and arise from a woody base. The fleshy leaves are more or less stalked.{{clarify|reason=What is "stalked", in botanical terms?|date=May 2024}} The rutty{{clarify|reason=Is "rutty" a reference to something being "full of ruts"—i.e., someone being 'stuck-in-a-rut'? How does this relate to petioles? Perhaps the word was "ruddy"?|date=May 2024}} [[petiole (botany)|petiole]] is 4 to 45 millimeters long. On the lower leaves it does not encompass the stem, but on the upper leaves it is clearly encompassing the stem.{{clarify|reason=By "encompassing", are you saying that the foliage "encompasses"—or otherwise obscures, hides, covers, conceals, etc.—the bulk of the plant (assuming it is a mature enough of a plant to do so)? The word encompassing is a bit vague here.|date=May 2024}}

The [[leaf blade]] may be broad, elliptical, elongate or oval in shape, with a green to deep, ruby-red (in full sun) hue. Leaves measure between 12–33 cm (5-13") long and between 7–20 cm (3-8") wide. The leaf tip is generally rounded or blunt. The base of the lower leaves is heart-shaped, that of the upper is wedge-shaped. The leaf margin is roughly notched, with a wavy edging, sometimes with one or several bluntly jagged lobes.<ref>[http://pza.sanbi.org/kalanchoe-sexangularis Kalanchoe sexangularis N.E.Br.] by South African National Biodiversity Institute, from PlantZAfrica.com</ref>

===Inflorescences===
A winter-bloomer, ''K. sexangularis''<nowiki/>' [[inflorescence]] consists of flat-topped [[panicles]] up to 30 cm (11.8") in length. The upright, green-yellow to bright yellow flowers are on 2–7 mm long [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncles]].

The green [[calyx (botany)|calyx]] tube is 0.5 to 2 millimeters long. The triangular, pointed calyx lobes are 1.5 to 2.2 millimeters long and about 1.2 millimeters wide. The pale pink, square-cylindrical to almost pyramidal [[corolla (botany)|corolla]] tube is enlarged in the lower half and 8 to 13 millimeters long. Their [[Salmon (color)|salmon-colored]], broadly egg-shaped to almost circular corolla lobes are narrowed or rounded at their tip and have a length of 2 to 4 millimeters and are 1.5 to 3 millimeters wide. The [[stamen]]s are attached to the tip of the corolla tube. Upper stamens protrude from the flower. The almost circular [[anthers]] are 0.4 to 1 millimeter long. The linear-lanceolate, pointed [[nectar]] flakes are 1.6 to 4 millimeters long. The [[carpel]] has a length of 6.5 to 10 millimeters. The [[stylus]] is 1.7 to 4 millimeters long.<ref>Bernard Descoings: Kalanchoe sexangularis. In: Urs Eggli (Ed.): Succulents Lexicon. Crassulaceae (thick leaf family). Eugen Ulmer, Stuttgart 2003, ISBN 3-8001-3998-7, pp. 182 .</ref>

The seeds reach a length of 1 to 1.3 millimeters.

==Distribution==
''Kalanchoe sexangularis'' is common in [[Zimbabwe]], [[Mozambique]] and [[South Africa]] on rocky slopes in the shade or partial shade of trees or shrubs in bushland.
